situated_beneficiary.support: "הכנסת רשאית, בהחלטה ברוב חבריה, להשעות מכהונתו את יושב ראש הכנסת או סגן ליושב ראש הכנסת או לקבוע סייגים לכהונתם; פרטים ייקבעו בחוק"
situated_beneficiary.note: Operative provision (new s.20(b)-(d) and s.20A(c1)) gives the Knesset general powers to restrict the election of, suspend, or remove the Speaker or any Deputy Speaker, with details left to statute. It has no single-instance, sunset, deadline or application clause and names no officeholder. I searched English and Hebrew web sources for 1997 press reports of a pending proceeding, indictment, AG opinion or petition against the then Speaker (Dan Tichon, signatory) or any Deputy Speaker. I also searched the NYU Faculty Digital Archive (Divrei HaKnesset), which has no session for the passage day. Nothing found. Bill (הצעות חוק 2582, 12.2.1997, p.170) not retrieved.

situated_beneficiary.support: Amendment: "מבקר המדינה יכהן תקופת כהונה אחת בלבד"; deleted s.8 tail: one who served "שתי תקופות בזו אחר זו לא יהיה מועמד" for the next term.
situated_beneficiary.note: The amendment lengthens the term from five to seven years, makes it a single term, and deletes the old s.8 bar on a third consecutive term. It has no transitional or application clause. The sitting Comptroller, Miriam Ben-Porat, was in her second consecutive term (re-elected 1993, per post-passage search snippets used only for that pre-passage fact). She was already barred from the next term under the old s.8, so the single-term rule leaves her position unchanged. No permitted source establishes that the seven-year term applied to her current term or moved its end date (item 3). I found no pending proceeding or formal step concerning her or the office. I searched English press and reference sources for 1998 reports on the amendment and the succession. Bill (הצעות חוק 2698, 9.3.1998, p.286) not retrieved.

situated_beneficiary.support: "בשנה שבה מתקיימות בחירות לכנסת ולראש הממשלה או בחירות מיוחדות לראש הממשלה, תקבע ועדת הכנסת את מספרם של הכנסים"
situated_beneficiary.note: The operative provisions move the rules on Knesset sessions to statute. They also let the Knesset Committee set the number, timing and length of sessions in any year of general or special prime-ministerial elections, below the eight-month minimum. At passage, a special prime-ministerial election was pending after Barak's resignation of 10.12.2000 (search snippets, Jewish Virtual Library / MFA). But the rule applies to every election year, binds the Knesset's session calendar rather than the government or an officeholder, and has no single-instance or sunset clause. It moves no deadline binding the government. I found no pending proceeding or formal step to which the enactment applies. Bill (הצעות חוק 2966, 20.12.2000, p.396) not retrieved.

situated_beneficiary.note: The amendment ends Knesset membership on a final conviction carrying moral turpitude without requiring a sentence of actual imprisonment. It applies only to MKs convicted on or after commencement. I searched for any MK with an indictment or trial pending on 9.7.2001 whose pending matter it would directly affect. (1) MK Mordechai (former Center Party leader) was convicted and given a suspended sentence before passage (search snippet, jweekly 4.5.2001). S.2 excludes him, so his position is unaltered. (2) MK Azmi Bishara: after his Syria speech of 10.6.2001, the AG's documented formal steps toward lifting his immunity date from 25.9.2001 (Adalah, search snippet), after passage. I found no pre-passage formal step. (3) English and Hebrew searches found no other sitting MK under indictment at passage. Bill (הצעות חוק 3012, 13.6.2001, p.715) not retrieved.

It deletes the tail of s.11(a)(2) from "לענין פיזור הכנסת" and exempts documents connected with forming a government from countersignature (s.12). It takes effect on the day of the 16th Knesset elections. These general rules bind whoever is President. I searched English press for a pending matter involving President Katsav (signatory) or government formation in October 2001 and found none. Bill (הצעות חוק 3027, 23.7.2001, p.764) not retrieved.

situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: The 32nd Government of Israel (Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu; Finance Minister Yuval Steinitz), formed 31.3.2009
situated_beneficiary.matter: That government's State Budget for 2009 (and 2010), not yet passed at the date of passage. Also the Basic Law: The Knesset s.36A deadline for passing it, failing which the Knesset is treated as dissolved.
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 4, and item 3. Item 4: the enactment is itself a temporary provision whose operative sections apply only to the 2009-2010 budget, the sitting government's own measure. Item 3: s.2 moves the s.36A 'determining day' for that budget to 107 days from the government's formation. S.1(a)(2) fixes 16.6.2009 as the latest date for the government to table it. Pre-passage press reported the government approaching a deadline of 45 days after the elections.
situated_beneficiary.fact_date: 2009-04-07 (enactment text). The deadline it moved was reported on 2009-04-04, and the government was formed on 2009-03-31.
situated_beneficiary.source: ס״ח תשס״ט 2196, עמ' 134 (7.4.2009), IA capture of fs.knesset.gov.il/18/law/18_lsr_301021.pdf. Israel National News, israelnationalnews.com/news/130758 (deadline of 45 days after the elections; proposal to extend). RTÉ News, 'Netanyahu sworn in as Israeli PM', rte.ie/news/2009/0331/115763-israel (formation date).
situated_beneficiary.support: s.2: "על אף האמור בסעיף 36א לחוק־יסוד: הכנסת, היום הקובע לגבי חוק התקציב הדו־שנתי יהיה 107 ימים מיום כינון הממשלה"
situated_beneficiary.note: The text as passed covers only 2009-2010. Later amendments that extended it to 2016 were not considered. deviations: Working folder: the sheet says to create a scratch subfolder for downloads, but the caller told me to write no files. I saved no downloads. Gazette PDFs were read in memory (macOS PDFKit via osascript, straight from Internet Archive URLs), and Wikisource wikitext went from curl to stdout. Because one Wikisource output (Basic Law: The Knesset, raw text) was long, the harness automatically saved it to its own tool-results file [path omitted when saved to the repository]. I read that file with grep and then refetched to stdout. No file in the research folder or repository other than the sheet was opened.

Source outside the permitted list: he.wikisource.org consolidated texts of Basic Laws: The President of the State, The State Comptroller, The Knesset, and the 2009-2016 State Budget law. I used them only to find each amendment's gazette PDF, to see which sections each amendment touched, and to read current s.42A for context. Every coding rests on the gazette text as published.

Numbering notes: Wikisource labels the seq 73 law 'תיקון מס׳ 6 [צ״ל: 5]', while the gazette title is 'תיקון מס׳ 6'. ס״ח 1809 p.2 also carries Basic Law: The Knesset Amendment No. 34, which I did not code. ס״ח תשס״ג p.524 carries two President amendments (No. 6, PDF 299861, and No. 7, PDF 299862). I coded seq 79 from No. 7 (the s.8 single-candidate rule), as the sheet's link specifies.

Not found: no bill explanatory notes (הצעות חוק) for any of the eleven rows were retrieved, because Knesset sites are geo-blocked and I did not locate Internet Archive captures. Divrei HaKnesset for the passage days was not consulted: an NYU Faculty Digital Archive search showed only selected sessions, none on these dates. Searchable pre-passage press for 1997-2003 was thin, so the No codes for seqs 54, 57, 61, 64 and 70 rest partly on the absence of results.

Post-passage sources used only for pre-passage facts, through search-result snippets: Ben-Porat's 1993 re-election (seq 57), Katsav in office since 31.7.2000 (seq 79), Barak's resignation on 10.12.2000 (seq 67). None of these decided a Yes.

Court outcomes that reached me through search-result snippets without my opening the page. (a) Seq 70 searches: snippets reported that MK Mordechai was convicted with a moral-turpitude finding and given a suspended sentence in 2001 (a pre-passage criminal matter, not one of these enactments). They also reported a 2008 sentence of MK Benizri. An Israel Democracy Institute commentary snippet said removing the imprisonment requirement was raised in light of Mordechai's sentence; that is commentary and was not used. A snippet also named a 2016 High Court petition about a later amendment to Basic Law: The Knesset (not in this batch); no outcome was read. (b) Seq 61 search: a 2024 commentary snippet referred to a High Court ruling limiting recess-session requests by 25 MKs. It concerns the recess-convening regime, not this enactment's validity. I did not open it. (c) Seq 64 and 67 searches: snippets on the Camp David negotiations and the February 2001 election results, which are not court outcomes.
Pages closed: none needed closing. No page describing a court's decision on any of these enactments was opened.
